name: Ethosuximide
metabolism: Ethosuximide is readily absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and extensively metabolised in the liver. It is widely distributed throughout the body but is not significantly bound to plasma proteins, so saliva concentrations may be useful for monitoring. Peak serum levels occur 1 to 7 hours after a single oral dose, with therapeutic levels between 40 and 100 mcg/ml. It has a long elimination half-life: 40-60 hours in adults and 30 hours in children. It is excreted in the urine mainly in the form of its metabolites.
summary: Ethosuximide is a succinimide medication used to treat absence seizures, either alone or with other antiseizure medicines.
